# Inventory

Read these rules before you change `npm-manifest.json`, its schema, or the manifest check. This page holds the full text of the live rules of the group, from [README.md](../README.md).

<a id="nr-70"></a>

## NR-70: The inventory universe `[HOLD]`

> The inventory universe is every source `package.json` at or below the workspace root.

Old number: 7.1.1.

Check: script.

Issues: I-01.

Discovery is
repository-aware — tracked files plus untracked-unignored ones — so ignore rules exclude installed and generated
trees without this rule enumerating names; `inventory.exclude` removes explicitly out-of-scope trees.

The validator's own package tree is tooling, excluded by its resolved installation path. A standalone entry
additionally includes its own `package.json` even when the parent repository ignores it. Discovery never derives its
set from `workspaces`, names, `private` or kind — members, non-members, standalone projects and non-packages are all
in scope; a `package.json` outside the workspace root or inside an ignored tree without a standalone entry is not.

```text
# ✅ Both files are in scope; being outside workspaces does not hide the second one.
package.json
examples/standalone/package.json

# ✅ The validator identifies and excludes its own autonomous package tree.
<validator-installation>/package.json

# ✅ A separately managed tree is excluded explicitly, including all of its descendants.
"inventory": { "exclude": ["./separately-managed-sdk"] }

# ✅ Ignore rules exclude generated and installed trees without hard-coding their names here.
node_modules/dependency/package.json           # ignored dependency installation
cache/tool/package.json                        # ignored generated cache
tarballs/unpacked/package.json                 # ignored release output

# ✅ An explicit standalone entry includes its own ignored root manifest, but not its generated children.
examples/standalone/package.json               # included
examples/standalone/cache/package.json         # still ignored

# ❌ Discovering only workspace members misses valid non-member package.json files.
package.json -> workspaces[]

# ❌ A fixed prune list becomes incomplete whenever another tool creates a differently named output tree.
prune = ["node_modules", ".git"]
```

## NR-71: Classify every manifest exactly once `[GAP]`

> `npm-manifest.json` classifies every in-scope manifest exactly once.

Old number: 7.1.2.

Check: script.

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: write the key "./common" twice in npm-manifest.json#packages with different kinds: JSON.parse keeps the second, every check passes, and the file classifies one directory twice. Fix: issue I-115.

Issues: I-01, I-115.

An entry records the package kind
and the inventory facts that `package.json` cannot express, such as dev-to-published ownership, dependency grouping
and mirroring.

```jsonc
// ✅ Manifest fragment keyed by the directory relative to the workspace root.
"./family/active/pkg": { "kind": "published", "name": "@scope/library", "member": true }

// ❌ A package name is neither a filesystem identity nor guaranteed to be unique.
"@scope/library": { "kind": "published", "name": "@scope/library", "member": true }
```

<a id="nr-72"></a>

## NR-72: Inventory equals discovery `[HOLD]`

> The inventory and discovery sets are equal.

Old number: 7.1.3.

Check: script.

Issues: I-07.

The TypeScript validator canonicalizes the files found by [NR-70](../entries/NR-70.md),
removes the trees listed by `inventory.exclude`, adds each non-excluded explicitly declared standalone root, and
compares that set with `npm-manifest.json#packages`. A missing or stale key is a `7.1.3` error.

<a id="nr-73"></a>

## NR-73: Manifest paths stay inside their root `[GAP]`

> A manifest path never contains `.` or `..` as a segment and never escapes its declared root.

Old number: 7.1.4.

Check: script.

Evidence:

- Gap, wrong check: In a nested workspace with a valid local source, an unrelated escaping symlink at the same path under the repository root produces a false containment error; conversely a safe repository-root counterpart hides an escaping workspace source. Fix: issue I-116.

Issues: I-116.

The schema
enforces safe lexical forms for every path field; the validator additionally resolves each local path against its
declared root, follows symlinks with `realpath`, and rejects a result outside that root.

```jsonc
// ✅ Canonical paths stay below their documented roots.
"publishedRelPath": "./hardhat/v2/plugin/pkg"
"source": "./common-vendored/src"

// ❌ Traversal is rejected even when normalization would produce an in-tree path.
"publishedRelPath": "./hardhat/v2/../v3/plugin/pkg"
"source": "./common-vendored/../outside"

// ❌ A vendored filename is one basename, not a path or traversal segment.
"files": ["..", "nested/file.ts"]
```

<a id="nr-73a"></a>

## NR-73a: Do not assume the repository root `[VIOLATED]`

> The workspace root is not assumed to be the repository root.

Old number: 7.1.5.

Check: missing.

Evidence:

- `fhevm-npm/base/checks/inventory.ts:128-130` shows a vendored `source` resolved from the git root, and no test runs the checks with the workspace below the git root. Fix: issue I-55.

Issues: I-01, I-21, I-55.

The workspace may sit anywhere
inside its git repository, as in a monorepo. Every path the manifest or a rule names is relative to the workspace
root. The repository root serves git alone: reading commits and objects, and translating a workspace path into the
path a git command expects. A test runs the checks with the workspace one directory below the repository root.

```text
✅ <repo>/fhevm-mocks/common-vendored/src    "./common-vendored/src" from the workspace root
❌ <repo>/common-vendored/src                 the same path from the repository root
```

## NR-74: JSON Schema checks entry-local invariants `[GAP]`

> JSON Schema enforces entry-local invariants.

Old number: 7.2.1.

Check: script.

Evidence:

- Gap, loose check: tarballs.relPath: `./tarballs/../../outside` passes both (see NR-73). Fix: issue I-117.

Issues: I-01, I-117.

It validates canonical keys, field shapes, package-kind
constraints, safe lexical paths and mirror repository URLs. It also reserves `.` for the workspace root and restricts
ownership metadata to the kinds that can carry it.

## NR-75: The validator checks external and graph invariants `[HOLD]`

> The TypeScript validator enforces external and graph invariants.

Old number: 7.2.2.

Check: script.

It compares entries with real
`package.json` files and `workspaces`, resolves `publishedRelPath`, checks one dev owner per published package, and
requires the conventional scripts selected by each entry's capabilities. Each check is its own `fhevm-npm check` command
and does not prove [NR-72](../entries/NR-72.md) itself: run alone, it does not discover packages the manifest omits. `make check-pre` runs
`fhevm-npm check manifest-coverage` ([NR-72](../entries/NR-72.md)) before the checks of this rule and stops at the first failure, so the gate
runs them only on a complete inventory.

> **Implemented.** `fhevm-npm check manifest-coverage` performs repository-aware discovery, excludes its own autonomous package
> tree and the paths listed by `inventory.exclude`, adds explicit standalone roots, compares the result with the
> manifest and checks realpath containment.
